title: Comprehensive Income & OCI
description: Understand net income, other comprehensive income and accumulated other comprehensive income.
html:
Net income is not always the whole story

Certain gains, losses and other items are recognized outside net income and instead enter Other Comprehensive Income, or OCI.

Comprehensive Income = Net Income + Other Comprehensive Income

OCI vs AOCI

OCI

Other Comprehensive Income relates to qualifying items recognized during the period.

AOCI

Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income is the cumulative balance reported within equity.

Simple example

Assume:

Net Income $200,000
Other Comprehensive Income $30,000
$200,000 + $30,000 = $230,000 Comprehensive Income

What types of items can appear in OCI?

Depending on the applicable accounting guidance, OCI can include certain items involving:

  • Certain unrealized gains and losses on debt securities
  • Certain foreign currency translation adjustments
  • Certain pension and postretirement benefit adjustments
  • Certain gains and losses associated with qualifying cash flow hedges

Why AOCI matters

OCI is a period measure.

AOCI represents accumulated OCI amounts reported as a component of stockholders' equity.

Simple AOCI roll-forward

Beginning AOCI = $15,000

Assume current-period OCI increases AOCI by $8,000, with no other AOCI adjustments in this simple example.

$15,000 + $8,000 = $23,000 Ending AOCI

Reclassification

Some amounts initially recognized in OCI can later be reclassified into net income when the applicable accounting requirements are satisfied.

This prevents simply treating every OCI amount as permanently excluded from net income.

Keep the three concepts separate

Net Income — income statement measure.

OCI — qualifying current-period items outside net income.

AOCI — cumulative equity balance associated with OCI.
